questions.subject: science
questions.question: Which of the following is a fundamental unit?
questions.explanation: Kilogram measures mass. It is a basic SI unit, so it is a fundamental unit.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Which of the following physical quantities has the unit m/s^2?
questions.explanation: Acceleration means change in speed. Its unit is m/s^2.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Which of the following is a derived unit?
questions.explanation: Joule measures work or energy. It is made from other units, so it is a derived unit.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Which of the following units denote newton?
questions.explanation: Newton is the unit of force. Force uses kg, m and s, so newton is kg m s^-2.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: What does scientific study mainly include according to the chapter?
options: Scientific facts, theories, models, experiments and physical situations
questions.explanation: Scientific study uses facts, models and experiments. It helps us understand nature in a planned way.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: What does scientific study investigate in a planned and organized way?
questions.explanation: Scientific study investigates natural objects. It studies them in a planned and organized way.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Why do we become curious when we see a phenomenon or change?
options: To know why it happens and what factors are involved
questions.explanation: Curiosity makes us ask why a change happens. It also helps us find the factors involved.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: In scientific research, what is usually present for each incident or change?
options: Only one fixed answer without testing
questions.explanation: In science, every change has a cause and a result. This is called cause and effect.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: In Activity 1.1, which variable is changed by stretching the rubber band to different lengths?
questions.explanation: The rubber band extension is changed by the researcher. So it is the changed variable in this activity.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: In Activity 1.1, which variable depends on the extension of the rubber band?
options: Distance travelled by the paper bullet
questions.explanation: The paper bullet distance changes when the extension changes. So distance depends on the rubber band extension.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: In the catapult activity, which variables are controlled?
options: Thickness of rubber band and size of paper bullet
Colour of paper and time of day
Number of students and classroom size
questions.explanation: These are kept the same in each trial. Keeping them the same makes the test fair.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Which type of variable is manipulated or changed by the researcher?
questions.explanation: An independent variable is changed by the researcher. It is changed to see its effect.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Which type of variable cannot be changed directly but is determined from another variable?
questions.explanation: A dependent variable is the result we measure. It changes because of the independent variable.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Why are controlled variables kept the same during an experiment?
options: To make the result valid, reliable and accurate
To change the independent variable many times
questions.explanation: Controlled variables are kept the same. This makes the experiment fair and reliable.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: How many independent variables should usually be present in one research or experiment?
questions.explanation: Only one independent variable is usually used. Then we can know what caused the result.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: How many dependent variables should usually be present in one research or experiment?
questions.explanation: Usually one dependent variable is measured. This helps us study one result clearly.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: While writing the relation between variables in an equation, where is the dependent variable usually written?
options: On the left side of the equation
On the right side of the equation
questions.explanation: The dependent variable is written on the left side. The right side shows the things it depends on.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: While plotting a graph, where is the dependent variable usually plotted?
questions.explanation: The dependent variable is plotted on the y-axis. The x-axis usually shows the independent variable.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Into how many types are physical quantity units divided in this chapter?
questions.explanation: Units are divided into two types. They are fundamental units and derived units.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Which is the correct pair of the two types of units?
questions.explanation: The two unit types are fundamental and derived. Fundamental units are basic, and derived units are made from them.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: What is a fundamental unit?
options: A unit that depends on many other units
A unit that has independent existence and cannot be resolved into simpler units
A unit used only in chemistry
A unit formed only from force
questions.explanation: A fundamental unit is a basic unit. It does not come from other units.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: What is the SI fundamental unit of length?
questions.explanation: Metre measures length. It is the SI fundamental unit of length.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: What is the SI fundamental unit of time?
questions.explanation: Second measures time. It is the SI fundamental unit of time.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: What is the SI fundamental unit of temperature?
questions.explanation: Kelvin measures temperature. It is the SI fundamental unit of temperature.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: What is the SI fundamental unit of electric current?
questions.explanation: Ampere measures electric current. It is the SI fundamental unit of current.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: What is the SI fundamental unit of luminous intensity?
questions.explanation: Candela measures luminous intensity. It is a SI fundamental unit.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: What is the SI fundamental unit of amount of substance?
questions.explanation: Mole measures amount of substance. It is the SI fundamental unit for this quantity.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: What is a derived unit?
options: A unit formed by combining fundamental units
A unit that cannot be expressed in symbols
A unit that is always independent
A unit used only for length
questions.explanation: A derived unit is made by joining fundamental units. For example, m^2 comes from metre x metre.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Which is the derived unit of area?
questions.explanation: Area means length x breadth. So its unit becomes m^2.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Which formula is used for area in the chapter?
questions.explanation: Area is found by length x breadth. This gives the space covered by a surface.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Which is the derived unit of volume?
questions.explanation: Volume means space occupied by an object. Its unit is m^3.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Which formula is used for density?
questions.explanation: Density means mass in a given volume. So density = mass/volume.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Which is the derived unit of velocity?
questions.explanation: Velocity means distance travelled per second in a direction. Its unit is m/s.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Which is the derived unit of acceleration?
questions.explanation: Acceleration means change in velocity per second. Its unit is m/s^2.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Which formula is used for force according to the chapter?
questions.explanation: Force is found by mass x acceleration. So the formula is force = mass x acceleration.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Which derived unit is represented by N?
questions.explanation: N stands for newton. Newton is the derived unit of force.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Which formula is used for pressure?
questions.explanation: Pressure means force on a given area. So pressure = force/area.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Which formula is used for work?
questions.explanation: Work is done when force moves an object through distance. So work = force x distance.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Which derived unit is represented by W?
questions.explanation: W stands for watt. Watt is the derived unit of power.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Which physical quantity has the derived unit Hz in the table?
questions.explanation: Hz stands for hertz. Hertz is used to measure frequency.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Why is unit analysis used in science?
options: To check validity and uniformity of equations
To remove units from all answers
To change all units into grams only
questions.explanation: Unit analysis checks if an equation is valid. It compares units on both sides.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: What condition must be satisfied for a physical equation to be valid by unit analysis?
options: Units on both sides must be the same
Only numbers must be the same
The equation must have no variables
questions.explanation: A valid equation must have the same units on both sides. If units are different, the equation is wrong.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Why is v^2 = u^2 + 2as a valid equation in the chapter example?
options: Both sides have the same unit m^2 s^-2
questions.explanation: In this equation, both sides have unit m^2 s^-2. So the equation passes unit analysis.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Why is the relation s = v/t not valid according to unit analysis?
options: The right side does not have the same unit as displacement
The left side has no unit
questions.explanation: Displacement has unit metre. But v/t does not give metre, so the relation is not valid.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Why is m + 1/s not allowed as a physical addition?
options: Because the two terms have dissimilar fundamental units
Because both terms are measured in metre
Because second is not a unit
Because m and s are the same quantity
questions.explanation: We can add only similar units. Metre and 1/second are different, so they cannot be added.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: What happens if different rubber bands are used in each trial of Activity 1.1?
options: The controlled variable changes and the result may not be valid
The experiment becomes a unit analysis
questions.explanation: If rubber bands change, the controlled variable changes. Then the result may not be fair.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: In an experiment on plant growth, which factors are listed as independent variables in the chapter?
questions.explanation: Sunlight and water are changed to see their effect on plant growth. So they are independent variables.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: In the example of dissolving sugar, what is the controlled variable?
options: Amount of water kept at 100 grams
questions.explanation: The amount of water is kept the same. So it is a controlled variable.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: If more than one independent variable changes together, what problem can occur?
options: It becomes difficult to draw a valid conclusion
questions.explanation: If many variables change together, we cannot know the real cause. So the conclusion becomes difficult.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: In the rubber-band relation, if distance is denoted by x and extension by e, what relation is given?
options: x is directly proportional to e
x is inversely proportional to e
questions.explanation: Directly proportional means both increase together. More extension gives more distance.
